motif.name: World Ash
motif.description: Passages of the piano score that match one melody, in levels by how close they are to it. Level 1 is the closest. A run of repeated notes counts as one note. Passages that overlap, or lie within 1 measure of each other, are joined into one; the level is that of the closest.

source.author: Stewart Spencer and Barry Millington (eds.)
source.title: Wagner's Ring of the Nibelung: A Companion

levels.label: Original
levels.name: The melody as given
levels.description: The melody as you gave it. It is not a passage of the score.

levels.name: Closest to the original
levels.description: The best partial matches of the whole phrase. The pitches and the rhythm are the same, in any octave.

levels.name: Same core pitches
levels.description: Notes 1 to 7 of the phrase have the same pitches, in any octave, but the rhythm differs. In a sung passage the score may have one short extra note between two of them: it is skipped.

occurrences.label: The original
occurrences.note: The melody as you gave it, one octave higher, engraved from your notes. It starts with a pickup of one quarter note, the bars are in 6/4, and the score has a treble clef and 6 flats in the key signature. It is not a passage of the score.

occurrences.label: Same pitches, sung, one note skipped
occurrences.note: Your notes 1 to 7 (of 7) have the same pitches here, but not the same rhythm. In eighth notes, the score plays them as 3 4 1 3/2 3/2 1 1; yours are 2 2 3 1 4 2 8. The passage is sung, and the score has E♭ of 1 eighth note between your notes 3 and 4 in the same line. The voice has no staff of its own, so this note is left out of the match.
